transcript.text:
Thank you all for your reports. Let me summarize where we stand and what I'm prepared to decide.

First, Theo has confirmed a substantiated retaliation finding based on corroborated witness evidence, with a minimum corrective action of a final written warning under our protocol.

Second, Nadia has reported that the complainant has agreed to transfer to the Product Compliance team under the Chief Compliance Officer, and has requested that the manager have no direct supervisory contact for 90 days.

Third, Elias has flagged that because the manager is director-level and the retaliation finding is substantiated, our audit-committee charter requires notice to the Audit Committee before this investigation can be closed. That means we cannot close today without that notice.

Fourth, Ruth has flagged that our EPL policy requires written insurer notice and written consent before we admit liability or provide any monetary resolution.

Based on all of this, here is what I am prepared to approve as the closure package, subject to the conditions we've identified:

- The finding will be 'substantiated retaliation.'
- The corrective action will include at minimum a final written warning, consistent with Theo's protocol requirement.
- The complainant will transfer to the Product Compliance team under the Chief Compliance Officer.
- The manager will have no direct supervisory contact with the complainant for 90 days.
- We will provide notice to the Audit Committee before closing, per Elias's compliance flag.
- We will provide written notice to our EPL insurer and obtain written consent before finalizing any monetary resolution, per Ruth's insurance requirement.

Does anyone have additional input or objections before I formalize this?

Subject to the Audit Committee notice and insurer consent conditions Elias and Ruth have identified, HR is prepared to execute on this package.

transcript.text: I have no objections to the closure package as outlined, Marisol. From an insurance perspective, I want to clarify one important point: the EPL policy requirement for written insurer notice and written consent applies specifically before we admit liability or provide any monetary resolution. The corrective-action steps — the final written warning, the transfer, and the 90-day no-contact condition — are operational measures that do not, in themselves, constitute an admission of liability or a monetary resolution. However, if any component of this package evolves to include a monetary element — for example, a settlement payment, a severance arrangement, or any other financial consideration connected to this investigation — we must pause and obtain written insurer consent before finalizing that component. I recommend we document in the closure file that the EPL insurer has not yet been given written notice of this matter, and that any future monetary resolution is contingent on obtaining written insurer consent. I would also recommend we provide written notice to the insurer now, as a precautionary measure, so that if a monetary resolution becomes necessary we are not delayed by the consent process. Subject to that clarification, insurance is prepared to support this package.
